cells.tense: What matters is arriving in you before the argument for it does.
cells.act: give the mess a shape it can be carried in
cells.ask: Take something you are in the middle of, set a date and a place on it, and work only that. Hold the date even if the shape stays unclear.
cells.core:
You can read a half-lit situation and move on what you are reading. There is a piece of your life you have left open rather than force it into clarity, and you have been going a step at a time on only the light that step gives. When people bring you their mess, you tend to hand it back a little more sorted than it came.
Here is the growth. Among what you are holding open, pick the piece you would like to move. Put a date and a place on that one, and work it. The others can stay undecided; some will get heavier for the waiting, and you can decide then. The date is what makes the choice visible, and a decision does not have to close the whole picture to count.
cells.sheetLine: Put one date on one piece, and leave the rest open.
cells.verb: seeing the one thing that matters before you can say why
cells.place: in the fog with just enough light for the next step

cells.tense: The next step keeps getting postponed until the whole road is lit.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Face what you actually want, and this week take a step toward it you would take even if nothing else made sense yet. One move, then stop.
cells.core:
When you do not have the whole picture, you keep gathering. Another angle, one more fact that would make the choice obvious — and each load makes the weighing heavier, so you wait for a clear light before taking the step the fog already allows. The gathering feels like care. From outside it reads as standing still while the picture stays exactly as dim as it was.
The way out is smaller than the situation. Face what you really want, out of everything you have been holding, and turn toward it this week with a step you would take even if nothing else made sense yet. Not a plan, and not a decision about the whole road. One move, then stop. The move will tell you something the gathering cannot.
cells.sheetLine: The gathering feels like care and looks like standing still.

cells.tense: At a door you already walked through, you keep asking whether it was the right one.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: Each day this week, choose something minor on what you can see, and do not ask anyone for a second opinion. Notice how it turns out.
cells.core:
You no longer trust what you read in a situation without someone confirming it first, and the confirming makes the whole picture dimmer — which is why a minor decision can feel like the largest thing around. What you can see is still there; you have been handing it over for a second opinion before using it.
Start using it without the confirmation. Once a day, pick something minor and go with what you can see — no following it down the hall, no asking anyone first. Some of it will be wrong, and that is allowed, since the point is the using and not the score. It will feel thin. A week of walking on your own legs is how they come back.
cells.sheetLine: Decide one thing today on what you can see, and keep walking.

cells.tense: The conclusions arrive already reached, and you file them under luck.
cells.act: give back what is owed, and take what is yours
cells.ask: The next time someone credits you for a call you made, accept it plainly and say what you saw. Do not hand it back and do not overstate it.
cells.core:
You flag it as instinct, a hunch, going with your gut, and the calls keep turning out right. What you do is see the one thing that matters and then leave that out of the account, the same way you leave someone else out of a good outcome. So the times you saw clearly get filed under circumstance, and the times you did not get filed under your judgment. The record is off by however many good calls you have declined.
Next time someone credits you for one, accept it and say what you saw out loud. Not a speech — one sentence. Being seen is the small correction: you give your own perception the weight it has been carrying, and let someone agree with a call you would have put down to a good day.
cells.sheetLine: The calls you file under instinct are the ones you are making.
cells.verb: seeing the one thing that matters before you can say why
